passage: When Saurabh arrived in the small town of Hanagal as the new co-op officer, everyone liked him. He remembered names, brought sweets for the office and praised Sangeeta's accounts on his first day. By the third month, things had shifted. He expected the best chair at every meeting and his tea brought to his desk first. When the co-op's farm-loan scheme won praise from the district, he took the stage alone, though Sangeeta had designed it. When she mentioned her mother was in hospital, he said, "Yes, yes, anyway, about my report." He could still be warm, but mostly when the district officer was visiting.

qa.q: What does Saurabh's "Yes, yes, anyway, about my report" suggest about him?
qa.a: It suggests he shows little interest in Sangeeta's feelings and cares mostly about his own work and image.

qa.q: What turning point shows the change in Saurabh, and what does it cost the office?
qa.a: Taking the stage alone for a scheme Sangeeta designed showed his charm turning into credit-taking, which leaves colleagues feeling used.

qa.q: How might Sangeeta feel when he brushes off her mother's hospital stay?
qa.a: She probably feels hurt and unseen, and may start to resent his early compliments.

grounding: A charming new officer comes to expect special treatment, takes credit and shows little interest in a colleague's feelings unless it serves him.

passage: When Amara moved into the Toronto flat, Nour thought she'd found the perfect flatmate. Amara cooked jollof for the whole building, laughed at every story and called Nour "my sister" within a week. By winter, the pattern was clear. Amara used Nour's laptop without asking because her own was "too slow for important things". She told their friends the house party had been her idea, though Nour had planned every detail. When Nour cried after a bad job interview, Amara glanced up from her phone and said, "You'll be fine. Did you see what my boss said about my presentation?" Only when Amara needed a favour did the old warmth come back, sudden and bright.

qa.q: What did Amara cook for the whole building?
What does Amara's reply after Nour's bad interview suggest about her?
qa.a: It suggests she feels little concern for Nour's hurt and turns the attention back to herself.

qa.q: What turning point showed Amara's charm had changed, and why does it matter?
qa.a: Taking credit for the party Nour planned showed the charm had turned into entitlement, making the friendship one-sided.

qa.q: How might Nour feel when the old warmth comes back only when Amara needs a favour?
qa.a: She probably feels used and confused, unsure which Amara is real.

grounding: A charming flatmate comes to expect special treatment, takes credit and shows interest in her friend only when it serves her.
